title: Ichiran Releases At-Home Ramen Booth
paragraphs: At most ramen restaurants in Japan, customers sit side by side, with little privacy as they eat their noodles.
But at the Ichiran restaurant chain, customers have their own private spaces to enjoy their meal.

Customers sit at a long counter, with partitions separating each seat. Ramen is served through an opening in front of each customer, and it can be covered by a bamboo screen. This way, customers can enjoy their meal without being disturbed by other people — even the staff.
Ichiran calls these seats "Flavor Concentration Booths."
Now, the chain has released a miniature version of its famous booths that people can set up on a table or desk at home.
The kit includes partitions and signs like those found at Ichiran restaurants. It even has a working bamboo screen that can be moved up and down!
The home booth is small — it's only 33 centimeters high — but there's enough space to pass a bowl of ramen through the opening at the front.

At Ichiran restaurants, customers can use a button to call staff when they need help, or to order extra noodles if they still have soup left. The home booth has its own button too, and it plays the same chime that you can hear in Ichiran restaurants.
Of course, you'll still have to prepare and serve the noodles yourself!

The Flavor Concentration Booth kit was released on November 4 as part of the 10th anniversary of Ichiran's take-home ramen, which first went on sale in 2016. The kit comes with five servings of take-home ramen for 3,500 yen — about $22 — or 10 servings for 4,527 yen, or about $28.
It might not come with a ramen chef, but for Ichiran fans, it could be the next best thing to eating at the restaurant!
